notes: Legacy settings matrix for the Modes retirement. `settings` is the persisted frontend settings subset the legacy resolver consumed. `compare` lists resolver fields that have a home after the migration; probes with an empty list document fail-closed or release-noted divergence and carry beforeExpected/afterExpected assertions instead.

cases.description: Global custom mode G with exact-fit globals. Everyday-bound, unbound, builtin-bound and profile-override profiles; model and language have no profile home.
Several profiles for one bundle id: mode comes from the first profile, each override from the first profile that supplies it, IDE context from the first profile only.
Profiles bound to a disabled custom mode, a missing custom mode and a non-existent builtin id fail closed today. After migration they are unbound and follow their profile and the original globals.
A profile writing style of inherit or null falls through to the bound mode; an explicit style wins; duplicates fall through per field.
Profile-bound project-context mode enables IDE context only when the profile has roots.
Unbound profiles follow the global terminal mode today; after migration they carry its values. No-profile apps lose the style (release note).
Unbound profiles follow the global technical mode today; after migration they carry its values. No-profile apps lose the style (release note).
Unbound profiles follow the global messages mode today; after migration they carry its values. No-profile apps lose the style (release note).
An unbound profile with roots under a global project-context mode gets IDE context today. The migration writes nothing for it (release note).
Profiles whose effective mode is not G are pinned to the original global value wherever it decides the result, then the globals take G's values.
A global activeModeId naming a disabled mode already resolves to Everyday on load.
Builtin Terminal forces CLI formatting; a profile override beats it; custom modes carry boolean fields.
G's modelId is adopted only when installed; its language still is.
No custom modes, Everyday active: the migration changes nothing.
